title: Тонкие нитки
author: Лев Толстой
summary: A man demands ever finer thread, and is sold thread no one can see. Complete fable.

source.editionId: First Russian Book for Reading, Тонкие нитки; Wikisource revision 5737293

rights.original: Tolstoy (died 1910); underlying Russian work is public domain.
rights.transcription: Russian transcription from Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA; source page links to its revision history and terms.
rights.translation: New English translation for Slovarchik, CC BY-SA 4.0; no published translation reused.

translationReview.method: Checked all six sentences against the pinned source. Kept «тонкие» as one word in English throughout, since the spinner’s trick turns on the customer’s own demand being repeated back to him.

sentences.ru: Один человек заказал пряхе тонкие нитки.
sentences.en: A man ordered fine thread from a spinning woman.

sentences.ru: Пряха спряла тонкие нитки, но человек сказал: «Нитки не хороши, мне нужны нитки самые тонкие».
sentences.en: The spinner spun fine thread, but the man said: “This thread is no good, I need the very finest thread there is.”

sentences.ru: Пряха сказала: «Если тебе эти не тонки, так вот тебе другие», и она показала на пустое место.
sentences.en: The spinner said: “If these are not fine enough for you, then here is some other thread,” and she pointed at an empty space.
He said he could not see it.

sentences.ru: Пряха сказала: «Оттого и не видишь, что очень тонки; я и сама не вижу».
sentences.en: The spinner said: “That is just why you cannot see it — it is very fine; I cannot see it myself.”

sentences.ru: Дурак обрадовался и заказал себе еще таких ниток, а за эти заплатил деньги.
sentences.en: The fool was delighted, ordered more thread of the same kind, and paid good money for this.
